archetypes.name: phase1-api-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan calls specific Phase-1 functions by name and signature; type mismatches (run_id int vs str, StepResult vs Outcome enum, unplanned Runner-routed commands) would silently break at runtime with no lint signal.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that every Phase-1 function, class, and constant the plan references actually exists in python/gh.py, python/git.py, python/agents.py, python/proc.py, python/outcomes.py, python/config.py, python/redact.py, and python/errors.py with a compatible signature and semantics. Pay particular attention to type mismatches: CiStatus.failed_run_id is typed str|None but gh.failed_jobs and gh.run_view take run_id: int — confirm the plan addresses this conversion explicitly. Verify that the plan's use of 'result: outcomes.StepResult (OK/STALLED/TRANSIENT/NEEDS_USER_INPUT)' is consistent with how StepResult wraps an Outcome enum rather than holding a raw string. Check that all gh/git commands the plan intentionally routes through the injected Runner rather than gh.py/git.py wrappers (e.g., 'gh pr checks', 'git fetch', 'git diff --name-only', 'git add') are explicitly labelled as Runner-routed in the plan and that this matches the Phase-4 precedent the plan cites. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: shell-parity-constants
archetypes.rationale: The plan claims specific numeric limits and the CI_FIXABLE_JOBS set are in parity with the shell scripts; a silent value mismatch would mis-cap the loop or mis-classify jobs without any test catching it.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/ci-decide.sh, scripts/ci-wait.sh, scripts/ci-failed-jobs.sh, and scripts/gh-run-logs.sh and verify that every numeric constant the plan adds to config.py (CI_MONITOR_MAX_ITERATIONS=50, CI_MONITOR_MAX_REBASES=20, CI_MONITOR_MAX_FIX_ATTEMPTS=10, CI_MONITOR_FIX_WATERFALL_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3, CI_MONITOR_TRANSIENT_RERUN_MAX=1, CI_MONITOR_STATUS_FAILURE_BAIL=3, CI_MONITOR_LOG_TAIL_LINES=100) matches the corresponding literal in the shell source. Verify every decide() decision-matrix row the plan lists maps to a real branch in ci-decide.sh — check for matrix cells present in the shell but absent from the plan's parity table or vice versa, and confirm whether 'merge is still allowed past each cap' is actually encoded that way in ci-decide.sh. Confirm the CI_FIXABLE_JOBS frozenset matches the fixable-job enumeration in ci-failed-jobs.sh exactly with neither additions nor omissions. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-claim-traceability
archetypes.rationale: The plan's Edge cases and Failure modes sections contain behavioral claims with no guaranteed test-case mapping; untested claims leave the riskiest invariants unverified at merge time.
archetypes.prompt_body: Cross-reference every behavioral claim in the plan's Edge cases and Failure modes sections against the named test cases in Testing strategy and Acceptance, flagging any claim with no corresponding test path. Pay particular attention to: the suspend-resilience rule ('a sleep window >60s is not charged to the budget') in poll_ci; the 'already_running does not consume the transient budget' rule in evaluate_failure; the 'merge is still allowed past each cap' invariant being independently tested for all three caps (iteration, rebase_count, fix_attempts) separately; the squash-merge race detection path in gather_status; the 'still in progress' deferral case in collect_failed_logs; and whether the test for 'verify-failed on attempt 1 then passing on attempt 2' explicitly asserts launch_fn call count equals 2. Also check whether the 'verify-failed on all 3 outer attempts → waterfall-failed (not local-unfixable)' path appears as a distinct named test case rather than being implied by a general cap test. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
